limitations: This is an operator-controlled discovery verification using isolated E2B sandboxes, not a scored answerer rerun, skill-adoption result, or benchmark score.

The 15 core live assertions pass, including exact unpatched reproduction, patched explicit list/search, scoped/default/builtin discovery, six nonempty hash-matched builtin procedure invocations, explicit nonexistent-root failure and local path/name rejection.

Live handler permission propagation is NOT verified. Both default and explicit-user SDK reads/listings return root-owned mode-000 fixtures, and patched list/search consequently return those fixtures. The two permission assertions remain failed and visible.

The permission fixtures are real: commands run as UID 1001 receive actual Permission denied errors for cat and ls. Their E2B CommandExitError objects are recorded, but they are not file-SDK errors and are not claimed as resource-handler permission propagation.

At the pinned base, protectCorpusSandbox forces command/mutation users but does not bind read/list. This probe leaves that code and the active run untouched; explicit SDK user:user alone did not enforce the observed POSIX read/list restrictions.
Builtin skill invocation returns installed procedure text and verifies its nonempty length and manifest SHA-256; no workflow described by that text is executed.
Only resource-handler discovery/invocation and these SDK/POSIX boundaries are exercised. No full runtime/broker/MCP/model loop, external provider procedure, or model-driven adoption is tested.
The template content digest is the actual image-manifest file SHA-256, not a whole-VM or immutable Ubuntu base-image digest; only the base label ubuntu:24.04 is available from that marker.

Missing builtin installations, transport failures and conflicting/misleading structured error signals remain covered by the existing focused mocked regression tests, not induced by modifying the live installed builtin bundle or provider behavior.
